newsitem.title: USA: Yemen criticized over demand for rhino horn.
newsitem.headline: Yemen criticized over demand for rhino horn.

text.p: The World Wildlife Fund accused Yemen on Wednesday of failing to do enough to halt trade in smuggled rhinoceros horn despite a 20-year international ban.
The horn is prized in Yemen for carving into the handles of traditional daggers.

A WWF report based on an undercover investigation said an average of 165 pounds (75 kg) of horn -- roughly equivalent to the horn of 25 African rhinos -- had been smuggled into Yemen in the last two years.

"Yemen may be singularly responsible for the death of more black rhinos than any other country in the last 20 years," Ginette Hemley, WWF director of international wildlife policy, said in a statement accompanying the report.
She called on the U.S. government and the international community "to use every available tool -- diplomatic, political and economic" to force Yemen to take stricter measures against the trade.

WWF said Yemen had taken important steps but should do more, including strengthening its laws, stepping up cooperation on the problem with African nations, promoting substitute materials for dagger handles and retraining craftsmen.
A spokesman for the Yemeni embassy in Washington, Ahmed Atef, said his government was doing its utmost to enforce the ban on rhino horn trade.
WWF said fewer than 2,500 black rhinos remain wild in Africa, compared to about 65,000 in 1970.
